facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration of 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration of 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
On 6 May 2012 the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, took part in the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.
According to the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, he did not take part in any disorder or clashes with the police at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
On 6 May 2012 the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, and his partner took part in the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.
When the police were dispersing the protestors at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, intervened in what he perceived as an arbitrary arrest of another protestor.
The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, was arrested at the site of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, was taken to the Ivanoskoye District police station in Moscow following his arrest on 6 May 2012.

At the Ivanoskoye District police station in Moscow, an on-duty officer drew up an administrative-offence record stating that the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, had disobeyed a lawful police order, an offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation.
The administrative-offence record stated that the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, had broken the police cordon and thrown stones and glass bottles.
The administrative-offence record stated that when ordered to cease his actions, the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, had refused to do so.
On 8 May 2012 the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, was brought before the justice of the peace of Court Circuit no. 100 of the Yakimanka District in Moscow.
The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, denied before the justice of the peace having broken the police cordon or having thrown bottles and stones at police officers.

The justice of the peace of Court Circuit no. 100 of the Yakimanka District in Moscow, relying on a police officer's report, found the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, guilty of disobeying a lawful police order under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation.
The justice of the peace of Court Circuit no. 100 of the Yakimanka District in Moscow sentenced the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, to fifteen days' detention.
On 6 February 2013 the first applicant's, Mr Gushchin's, flat was searched and his travel passport was seized.
On 6 February 2013 the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, was arrested on suspicion of having participated in acts of mass disorder during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
On 6 February 2013 the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, was arrested on suspicion of having used violence against the police during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.

On 28 April 2013 the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, was detained on suspicion of having participated in acts of mass disorder during the demonstration of 6 May 2012, an offence under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 28 April 2013 the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, was detained on suspicion of having used violence against the police during the demonstration of 6 May 2012, an offence under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 28 April 2013 the second applicant's, Mr Gaskarov's, pre-trial detention was ordered.

Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation of 30 December 2001, in force at the material time, provided that failure to obey a lawful order or demand of a police officer in connection with the performance of the officer's official duties relating to maintaining public order and security, or impeding the officer's performance of his or her official duties, shall be punishable by a fine of between RUB 500 and RUB 1,000 or by administrative detention for up to fifteen days.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered the organisers of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square to finish the meeting early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.

At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened a criminal investigation into suspected acts of mass disorder, an offence under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened a criminal investigation into suspected violence against the police, an offence under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 18 May 2012 the criminal investigation file opened on 6 May 2012 was transferred to the headquarters of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation for further investigation.
On 28 May 2012 another criminal investigation was launched into the offence of organising acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 28 May 2012 the two criminal cases concerning the events at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 were joined.
The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, remained in pre-trial detention for one year and six months.

The first applicant's, Mr Gushchin's, pre-trial detention was examined by the Court in a separate case and was found to be unjustified (see Kovyazin and Others v. Russia, nos. 13008/13 and 2 others, §§ 79-94, 17 September 2015).

The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment, calculated on the basis of a two-year prison term under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation running partly concurrently with a term of one year under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The first applicant's, Mr Gushchin's, pre-trial detention counted towards his prison sentence.
The second applicant's, Mr Gaskarov's, pre-trial detention counted towards his prison sentence.
On 2 July 2012 the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, lodged a complaint with the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation, alleging police brutality.
The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, attached to his complaint a medical certificate confirming the injuries caused to him on 6 May 2012.
The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, was not aware of any follow-up to his complaint of ill-treatment.
Ms L.A. witnessed a police officer kicking the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, in the face during the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.

The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, testified at trial that he had lodged a criminal complaint of ill-treatment with the law-enforcement authorities but they had refused to open a criminal investigation into his allegations.
